tasks.taskText: p-limit's limitFunction(function_, options) in index.js returns a function that runs function_ with limited concurrency, and its options accept rejectOnClear just as pLimit's do, but the returned function offers no way to discard the calls still waiting to run, so that option has no effect there. Today limitFunction(async () => 'done', {concurrency: 1}).clearQueue is undefined, and calling it throws "TypeError: limited.clearQueue is not a function". Give the returned function a clearQueue() method that discards the calls that have not started yet, exactly as clearQueue() does for a pLimit limiter: it returns undefined; calls already running are not cancelled and settle as usual; the function of a discarded call is never invoked; with rejectOnClear: true each discarded call's promise rejects with an error whose name is "AbortError", and without it (the default) the discarded promises stay unsettled; calls made after clearing run normally, and calls that are still running keep counting against the concurrency limit. For example, with const limited = limitFunction(async x => { await delay(40); return x * 2; }, {concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: true}), calling limited(1), limited(2) and limited(3) and then limited.clearQueue() gives 2 for the first call and AbortError rejections for the other two, whose function never runs. Clearing one limited function does not affect another one, even when both were made with the same options object, and clearQueue() on a limited function with nothing waiting is harmless. The TypeScript declarations in index.d.ts must describe the method: for const lf = limitFunction(async (_a: string) => 'ok', {concurrency: 1}), lf.clearQueue() must type-check with type void, and lf('input') must stay Promise<string>. What must not change: the limited function forwards all of its arguments and resolves with the function's result (or rejects with its error, a synchronous throw included); it never runs more than options.concurrency calls at once; invalid options still throw a TypeError (a concurrency of 0, a rejectOnClear that is not a boolean); and the default export pLimit, with its activeCount, pendingCount, clearQueue, concurrency and map, behaves as it does today. The source is index.js, with its type declarations in index.d.ts; the tests are test.js (ava) and the type tests index.test-d.ts (tsd). Add regression tests for this behaviour to the project's existing test suite. The project's tests run with npm test (xo, then ava, then tsd).

svgo's removeScripts plugin (plugins/removeScripts.js) removes scripting from an SVG: script elements, event attributes, executable attributes of HTML inside foreignObject, and links with an executable URL. A link is an <a> element whose href or *:href attribute is a javascript: or vbscript: URL, or a data: URL of an HTML, XHTML or SVG document; the plugin replaces such an element by its element children (its text children are dropped). Whether a URL is executable is decided by isExecutableUrl in lib/svgo/tools.js, which hasScripts in the same file also uses, so other plugins (cleanupIds, minifyStyles, removeHiddenElems, removeUselessStrokeAndFill) leave documents with executable links alone. Two kinds of executable link survive today. First, an SVG anchor written with a namespace prefix: in <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:svg="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink"><svg:a xlink:href="javascript:alert(1)"><rect width="1"/></svg:a></svg> the svg:a element is kept with its link, although it is an SVG <a>. Second, a URL whose scheme is split by ASCII tab, line feed or carriage return characters, such as href="java	script:alert(1)": browsers remove those characters from a URL before parsing it, so the link runs, but isExecutableUrl does not recognise it. Fix both. An element is an SVG anchor when its local name is a and it is unprefixed (as today) or its prefix resolves to the SVG namespace http://www.w3.org/2000/svg through the xmlns: declarations in scope at that element, counting declarations on the element itself and, where a prefix is redeclared on a descendant, the innermost one; an a element whose prefix resolves to another namespace is not an anchor and keeps its attributes and children. isExecutableUrl must ignore ASCII tab (U+0009), line feed (U+000A) and carriage return (U+000D) anywhere in the value, so that every user of it (removeScripts for links and for URL attributes of HTML inside foreignObject, and hasScripts) treats such a URL as executable: for example isExecutableUrl('java\tscript:alert(1)') and isExecutableUrl('data:text/ht\nml,x') must be true. What must not change: unprefixed anchors are handled as today; links with non-executable URLs (https: and relative URLs, #fragments, data:image/png and other inert data URLs, a scheme broken by a space) are kept; an anchor whose prefix resolves to another namespace is kept; script elements (prefixed or not, in the SVG or XHTML namespace), event attributes, and srcdoc, on* and executable URL attributes of HTML inside foreignObject are removed as today; and the output of every plugin, preset-default included, is unchanged for documents without such links. The plugin tests are fixture files test/plugins/<plugin>.<n>.svg.txt (a description, ===, the input, @@@, the expected output), run by test/plugins/_index.test.js. Add regression tests for this behaviour to the project's existing test suite. The project's tests run with npm test (vitest run, which also type-checks the JavaScript under tsconfig.json's strict checkJs).

ufo (URL utilities, TypeScript under src/, every module re-exported from src/index.ts) can add or overwrite query parameters with withQuery(input, query) and read them with getQuery(input), both in src/utils.ts, but it has no way to drop parameters selectively. Add, beside withQuery, and export from the package entry src/index.ts a function filterQuery(input: string, predicate: (key: string, value: string | string[]) => boolean): string that returns input keeping only the query parameters for which predicate returns true. Its rules: an input that contains no "?" is returned exactly as given (filterQuery("file:///C:/x", () => false) is "file:///C:/x", not normalized). Otherwise predicate is called once for each key of getQuery(input), in that order, with the decoded key and the value getQuery gives it (a string, or an array of strings for a repeated key, so a repeated key is kept or dropped as a whole), and the URL is rebuilt the way withQuery rebuilds it: filterQuery(input, () => true) equals withQuery(input, {}) for every input that contains "?"; protocol, auth, host, path and fragment are kept as withQuery keeps them; the kept parameters are encoded as withQuery encodes them; and the "?" is left out when no parameter remains. Examples: filterQuery("/foo?bar=1&baz=2", (key) => key !== "bar") is "/foo?baz=2"; filterQuery("/foo?bar=1", (key) => key !== "bar") is "/foo"; filterQuery("/foo?a=1&a=2&bar=3#frag", (key) => key !== "bar") is "/foo?a=1&a=2#frag"; filterQuery("https://example.com/p?q=%20x&bar=1", (key, value) => value !== "1") is "https://example.com/p?q=+x". What must not change: every existing export keeps its name and its behaviour for every input, in particular withQuery, getQuery, parseQuery, stringifyQuery, parseURL and stringifyParsedURL return exactly what they return today (for example withQuery("/x?bar", {}) stays "/x?bar", withQuery("/foo?", {}) stays "/foo" and withQuery("/p?x=1&&bar=2&", {}) stays "/p?x=1&bar=2"), and getQuery and parseQuery still return an object that does not inherit from Object.prototype and still ignore __proto__ and constructor keys. The tests are vitest files under test/, with the query utilities in test/query.test.ts. Add regression tests for filterQuery to the project's existing test suite. The project's tests run with npx vitest run --typecheck (npm test runs pnpm lint first; on the unchanged base under this install, prettier already reports src/punycode.ts, so lint is not part of the required test command).

ufo's withBase(input, base) and withoutBase(input, base) in src/utils.ts (exported from src/index.ts) decide whether input already starts with base by a plain string prefix test, after dropping a trailing slash from base. So a path whose first segment merely begins with the base's text is taken as being under the base: today withoutBase("/admin-dashboard", "/admin") returns "/-dashboard", withoutBase("/administrator", "/admin/") returns "/istrator", withBase("/admin-dashboard", "/admin") returns "/admin-dashboard" unchanged as if the base were already there, and withBase("/apix", "/api") returns "/apix". Fix both functions so that the base counts as present only when it ends at a boundary of input: input equals the base (without its trailing slash), or the character right after it is "/" or "?". When it is not present, withBase joins the base in front of input as it does for any other path (withBase("/admin-dashboard", "/admin") is "/admin/admin-dashboard", withBase("/a/bc", "/a/b/") is "/a/b/a/bc") and withoutBase returns input unchanged (withoutBase("/admin-dashboard", "/admin/") is "/admin-dashboard", withoutBase("/v10/items", "/v1") is "/v10/items"). What must not change: wherever the base does end at such a boundary, or input does not start with the base text at all, both functions return exactly what they return today, including a base followed by a query (withBase("/api?x=1", "/api") stays "/api?x=1", withoutBase("/api?test", "/api") stays "/?test"), a base equal to input (withoutBase("/base", "/base/") stays "/", withBase("/a/b", "/a/b") stays "/a/b"), nested paths (withoutBase("/admin/admin-dashboard", "/admin/") stays "/admin-dashboard"), an empty or "/" base, an input with a protocol given to withBase, and full URL bases (withoutBase("https://x.com/base/p", "https://x.com/base") stays "/p"); joinURL, withoutTrailingSlash, hasProtocol, isEmptyURL and every other export are unchanged. The tests are vitest files under test/, with these two functions in test/base.test.ts. Add regression tests for this behaviour to the project's existing test suite. The project's tests run with npx vitest run --typecheck (npm test runs pnpm lint first; on the unchanged base under this install, prettier already reports src/punycode.ts, so lint is not part of the required test command).
